About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Flight Controls Team

Our Flight Controls team is at the heart of Zipline’s product success - we are responsible for developing, testing and maintaining some of the critical flight software systems that enable our aircraft to complete missions autonomously, from takeoff through to predicting and executing a successful delivery, through to landing safely and accurately. We develop novel solutions to give us the responsiveness, robustness and quality we need to ensure our delivery platforms can function in a wide range of increasingly challenging conditions and truly serve everyone in the world equally.

The Role

Zipline’s people thrive on finding elegant solutions to complex problems, given what exists today and what we can develop to maturity quickly and confidently. We stay close to our customers, learn what really works, and find where we can put the leverage to make a big difference for them now.

As an intern on the Flight Controls team, you will learn how we fly autonomous aircraft in a range of challenging flight conditions. Using data from flight testing and simulation as well as our global fleet of customer aircraft, you will be looking for insights that can help improve our design. Through this you’ll have the opportunity to make changes to our systems that will measurably improve our product - your work will not just be theoretical; you will have the opportunity to see your contributions fly!

What You'll Do

- Contribute to the design, implementation, testing and release of innovative flight algorithms that improve the operational performance of our vehicle controllers

- Create tools and tests to demonstrate your design performance and protect against software regressions, using both theoretical guarantees and simulations

- Develop and improve simulation and other controls analysis tools so we can predict vehicle performance ahead of time and prove safety and reliability

- Analyze flight data to assess recent changes and upgrades, looking for regressions and potential areas for future improvement

- Design onboard integrity tests to communicate when the system performance is degraded

- Present key results and changes to the broader engineering team

What You'll Bring

- Your applied math skills stand out even among aerospace engineers.

- You think simulations and working with hardware are both fun.

- You have owned and developed controls solutions for a team project, thesis, or competition

- Exposure in one or more of the following areas: precision integrated inertial navigation, dynamic modeling of complex systems, linear control analysis, or optimal control with uncertainty.

- Software engineering skills, preferably with both embedded software (C, C++, Rust) and technical computing (MATLAB, python, Julia, etc.). Experience with Github and working in a multi-developer environment is an advantage.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January - April/May.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

Job Description

Are you an Engineer who wants to work on a large scale to drive significant business impact? Procter & Gamble is looking for people interested in different types of engineering: software, platform, or network to apply innovative technologies to business problems that require out of the box thinking. The work you will be doing could be anything from building data pipelines to feed Machine Learning models on petabytes of data that serve predictions globally, to building out consumer facing Internet of Things (IoT) Platforms, to building serverless applications to drive business needs from HR to Information Security. Regardless of the team, as a P&G IT Engineer you are someone who solves business problems using technology.

You are primarily a problem solver, comfortable writing code, debugging, and working hands-on. You can independently identify problems and their solutions. You are interested in continuously learning and developing your own breadth and depth of technical knowledge and its application. You have a solid foundation in Computer Science fundamentals. You take pride in the quality of solutions that you build and strive to make everything automated, testable, and scalable. You work collaboratively with others on your team and across different teams, are interested learning from others, and have a desire to share your knowledge with the broader internal engineering community.

Example Responsibilities by Role Type:

- Software Engineering: Translate system requirements and user stories into scalable, maintainable application designs and high-quality code. Develop, test, and validate solutions to ensure functionality, reliability, and performance. Implement and support code throughout the software development lifecycle, leveraging CI/CD tools for efficient integration and deployment. Collaborate closely with product, operations, and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless integration with dependent systems and services. Contribute to application architecture and technical design decisions as appropriate. Stay current with emerging software development practices, technologies, security standards, and vulnerability management.

- Network Engineering: Design, implement, and maintain network infrastructure solutions that support business objectives. Lead technology lifecycle planning, define technical requirements, validate new capabilities, and partner with suppliers to deliver effective solutions. Serve as an escalation point for critical network issues and play a key role in strategic projects, collaborating with operations teams and IT stakeholders to ensure reliable service and successful outcomes.

- Platform Engineering: Manage cloud platforms using configuration management to deliver secure, scalable, and automated solutions. Drive platform standards, resolve cloud and security incidents, and continuously improve engineering maturity across cloud services. Lead innovation through proof-of-concept initiatives, evaluate third-party cloud solutions, collaborate with service providers and product teams, and contribute to the Cloud Community of Practice to promote knowledge sharing, reusable code, and consistent standards across P&G.

As an intern, you will experience a subset of the above responsibilities

- You must be available during the summer of 2027 for a 12 week internship from mid/late May through early August.

- In process of obtaining a Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related technical/IT field.

- Strong problem-solving skills paired with experience in programming, such as Python, JavaScript, Java, C++, Go, etc. (Experience in a specific language is not required, will be expected to learn new languages).

- Strong understanding of network hardware and infrastructure such as routers, hubs, servers, VPNs, and switches.

- Ability to communicate technical concepts to teammates and non-technical colleagues.

Preferred:

- A history of solving hard problems with creative solutions.

- Experience with Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud Platform.

- Understand CI/CD and DevSecOps philosophies.

About the Service Tooling & Processes Team

Our team’s brief is to make maintenance better across Zipline. From designing smart fixtures that allow us to interact with our aircraft electronically to writing and validating maintenance procedures to kitting mobile maintenance vans that allow technicians to service our system in the summer heat, we aim to improve every aspect of maintenance. Our direct customers are the operational maintenance teams working on our systems in the field, and we’re laser-focused on making their lives better. If a maintenance technician working at 2 in the morning has everything they need to complete their work quickly, efficiently, and reliably, then we’ve done our job well.

The Role

As Zipline continues to rapidly iterate our hardware, we need to design, validate, and field new tools to allow technicians to do their work safely and efficiently. You’ll work closely with maintenance to understand their needs and pain points, then partner with hardware and tooling engineers to create solutions. Our team is based out of a high-volume test facility, so you’ll see your designs get immediate use, immediate feedback, and plenty of iteration cycles. Once those tools have been perfected at our test facilities they become part of our operational toolkits across all of Zipline and make real, tangible impacts on how we serve our customers.

What You'll Do

- Work closely with Hardware and Operations teams to understand pain points and process requirements.

- Design and prototype tools for drone and ground system maintenance. Use hand and machine tools to produce the first units.

- Gather operational feedback on your designs and iterate quickly.

- Partner with Operations leadership on trade studies to evaluate the optimal, fully-productionized forms of your design.

- Create usage documentation and lead training sessions as your designs roll out into operation.

What You'll Bring

- A strong grasp of mechanical design fundamentals (statics, dynamics, material properties, fabrication processes, etc).

- Proficiency with CAD software like NX, Solidworks, Fusion, etc.

- Hands-on prototyping experience like 3d printing, fabrications, welding, soldering, or assembly.

- Strong communication skills and an ability to collaborate cross-functionally.

- Obsessive customer focus and a drive to understand how your designs work in the real world.

- Ability to work on-site at our test facility in Esparto, CA every day.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our Esparto, CA Office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from (January 2027 - April 2027). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $37 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.
